name: Lukas Rinder
headline: Director of AI @ Tensordyne | AI Leader | TUM & CDTM | Ex-BMW

positions.title: Director of AI
positions.description: Promoted to team lead at Tensordyne, I now steer a dynamic team of 9 AI engineers. We specialize in converting floating-point precision neural networks into a format optimized for Tensordyne's advanced AI accelerator. Our key competency is the design and implementation of state-of-the-art post-training quantization (PTQ) and quantization-aware training (QAT) methods, maintaining task performance even under significant model compression. Our developments are bundled into an intuitive SDK, enabling customers to leverage the full capabilities of our accelerator. In parallel, we spearhead the mathematical innovations of our next-generation hardware.

positions.title: AI Software Engineer
positions.description: I continued to broaden my expertise at Tensordyne, orchestrating the efforts of the Munich office in the hardware-algorithm co-design for our next-gen chip. I pioneered improvements to our custom quantization and cluster compression schemes, leading to substantial accuracy enhancements in post-training quantization. Additionally, I delved into AI trends such as LLMs, Vision Transformers, and Diffusion Models to strategically prioritize potential support for our upcoming inference accelerator. My role included a three-month tenure at our Silicon Valley office, where I collaborated closely with our chip design team.

positions.title: Master's Thesis (Full Time)
positions.description: In my master's thesis, I devised a progressive model compression technique, merging quantization and knowledge distillation. This novel method enhanced the stability and accuracy of heavily compressed neural networks, becoming Tensordyne's standard for AI accelerator model conversion. I also proposed a novel contrastive knowledge distillation loss, inspired by contrastive learning. The thesis received the highest grade (1.0) in the German Grading System.

positions.title: AI Strategy Consultant

positions.title: AI Software Engineer (Part Time)
positions.description: As the fourth member of Tensordyne's Munich team, I tackled diverse AI development tasks, from model development to infrastructure work and network compression. Over time, my focus shifted to improving quantized neural network accuracy using quantization-aware training (QAT) and analyzing model stability under compression.

company.name: Tensordyne
company.tagline: Math, Chips, and Systems for AI Inference.
company.description:
Every leap in AI has followed the same pattern: first we made models bigger, then we tailored them, and now we let them think longer. 

Each step (scaling law) truly adds intelligence.

But in the end we land on the same runway: inference, and demand is exploding while power supply lags. 

We asked: what if the next step isn’t stacking another law on top, but a zeroth law beneath them all. A law that changes AI math. 

Because after all, AI is math, trillions of multiplies, and multiplication burns watts. 

Tensordyne uses logarithmic compute to turn multiplies into adds, cutting power at the root. 

We’ve cast our proprietary logarithmic math into custom silicon, hardware, interconnect, and system software. The result: one integrated system for multimodal GenAI inference designed for Hyperscaler and Neo Cloud data centers. 

What this means for our customers: With Tensordyne they can run the world’s largest multimodal models for thousands of users, with fewer racks, less power, and lower cost.

We’re well-funded and fast-moving, with co-headquarters in Sunnyvale, California and Munich, Germany, and a distributed team across North America and Europe.

Join us to change how the world runs Gen AI.
